title: The federation plugin is removed — a Corefile still naming it stops CoreDNS

detection.reason: read from the directive names the agent extracts off every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns, each scanned as its own Corefile (an AKS coredns-custom fragment included) — names only, never values; import lines are not followed

quote: The *federation* plugin (which allows for v1 Kubernetes federation) has been removed.
remediation: Delete the federation block from the Corefile before upgrading to 1.7. CoreDNS exits at startup on an unknown directive, taking cluster DNS down with it.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*federation\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line = the Corefile still loads the removed plugin

title: Metric names change wholesale — dashboards and alerts on coredns_*_count_total go dark

detection.reason: Prometheus rules and dashboards are not collected; the renamed series only exist at scrape time

quote: We mostly dropped `count` from `_total` metrics names:
remediation: Rewrite alert rules and dashboards from the pre-1.7 names (`coredns_dns_request_count_total`, `coredns_forward_request_count_total`, `coredns_cache_size`, …) to the new ones listed in the 1.7.0 notes; the old series stop being emitted the moment 1.7 starts.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("coredns_[a-z_]+_count_total|coredns_cache_size")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # rules printed reference pre-1.7 metric names and match nothing after the upgrade; also review Grafana dashboards outside the cluster

title: kubernetes: resyncperiod and upstream options are removed

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed

remediation: Delete `resyncperiod` and `upstream` lines from the kubernetes block before upgrading; CoreDNS 1.7 refuses to parse them and cluster DNS does not start.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(resyncperiod|upstream)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line inside the kubernetes block is rejected by 1.7

title: cache: DNSSEC (DO bit) is now set by default on cached lookups

detection.reason: request-time behaviour of the cache plugin; no Corefile option distinguishes the old default

remediation: Upstreams now receive DO-set queries from the cache; upstream resolvers that mishandle DNSSEC (or middleboxes that drop larger responses) surface as SERVFAILs after 1.7.1. Verify upstream behaviour with `dig +dnssec` before the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*cache\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed cache block queries upstream with DO set after 1.7.1

title: trace: debug-level tracing only when the debug plugin is active

detection.reason: logging volume is runtime behaviour; the projection carries the directive name only

quote: plugin/trace: Only with *debug* active enable debug mode for tracing - removes extra logging
remediation: Trace spans lose their debug detail unless the `debug` directive is also present; add it if you relied on that output.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(trace|debug)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # trace without a debug line prints less after 1.7.1
